newsitem.title: USA: Miami Computer sees merger boost revenues. [CORRECTED 12:30 GMT 14/6]
newsitem.headline: Miami Computer sees merger boost revenues. [CORRECTED 12:30 GMT 14/6]

text.p: Miami Computer Supply Corp said Friday it merged with a Georgia computer distributor, which could boost annual revenues to $100 million and earnings by five to eight percent.

"With this merger we should be able to increase our overall annualized revenue rate to over $100 million by the fourth quarter of 1997," said Michael Peppel, Miami's chief financial officer, in a statement. "Likewise, we believe the merger should add five to eight percent to our annualized earnings by the fourth quarter."
Miami said it signed a definite merger agreement with computer and office automation products distributor Data Associates Inc of Atlanta, which has $9 million in annual revenues.

Miami, which went public in November last year, reported a profit of $0.13 per share in the first quarter ended March 31, compared with $0.14 the previous year. Quarterly sales increased to $20.2 million from $12.6 million over the same period.
Miami Chairman Anthony Liberati said on May 2 he expected the company's full-year earnings to total about $0.52 per share. An April 3 First Call consensus put Miami's earnings at $0.50 per share.

Miami's president, Albert Schwarz (Corrects name of president from Philip Crone), said in a statement the Data Associates merger will expand the company's reach in the Southeast. Miami is a distributor of computer and office automation.
